CHAPTER IV
CUSTOMER DUE DILIGENCE

9. Customer Identification Procedure

9.1 Every regulated entity shall undertake identification of the customer at the
commencement of an account-based relationship, and shall record the officially
valid documents relied upon for that identification.

9.2 Where the customer is an individual, the regulated entity shall obtain the
following at the time of commencement:

(a) a photograph of the customer, captured either in person or through a live
video session conducted by an authorised official of the regulated entity;

(b) an officially valid document establishing identity and current address,
verified against the issuing authority's records where such verification is
technically available;

(c) the Permanent Account Number, or Form 60 where a Permanent Account Number
has not been allotted, validated against the database maintained by the income
tax authority.

10. Video-based Customer Identification Process

10.1 A regulated entity may undertake video-based customer identification as an
alternative to physical presence, subject to the safeguards in this section.

10.2 The video session shall be conducted in a live environment, and the
regulated entity shall ensure that the session is not a recording made at an
earlier time. The sequence of activities during the session shall be randomised
so as to establish that the interaction is genuinely live.

10.3 The recording of the video session shall be retained in a manner that
preserves its integrity, and shall be stored for a period of not less than five
years from the date of cessation of the relationship.

CHAPTER VI
RISK MANAGEMENT

16. Customer Risk Categorisation

16.1 Regulated entities shall categorise customers as low, medium or high risk
on the basis of an assessment carried out at onboarding and reviewed
periodically thereafter.

16.2 The assessment shall consider, at a minimum, the customer's identity, the
social and financial status declared, the nature of business activity, and
information about the customer's clients' business and their location.

(a) Customers categorised as high risk shall be subject to enhanced due
diligence, and the relationship shall not be activated until such diligence has
been completed and recorded by a designated compliance officer.

(b) Politically exposed persons, and customers for whom the source of funds
cannot be established from the documents furnished, shall be categorised as high
risk irrespective of the outcome of the general assessment.

16.3 The risk categorisation assigned to a customer, and the reasons supporting
it, shall be recorded and shall be made available to the internal audit function
and to the regulator on request.
